title: Polish cases at a glance
description: Why Polish nouns change their endings, and how to learn them without tables.

blocks.text: Polish nouns change their endings to show their role in the sentence. There are seven cases. You have already met several of them inside whole phrases: the accusative after poproszę and lubię (kawę), the genitive after do and after numbers from five (do pracy, pięć złotych), and the locative after w for places (w Krakowie). You do not need every table at once: learn the endings phrase by phrase, starting with the most frequent.

blocks.note: Accusative: the object of most verbs.
Genitive: after nie ma, after do, and after numbers from five.
Locative: after w and na for places.
